docs.title: Interactive Fiction Engine
docs.text: A Unity framework for building text-based narrative games.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Room-based world — Navigate between locations via exits
  • Object system — Items, containers, doors, characters
  • Natural language input — "take key", "open door", "go north"
  • Extensible actions — Add custom verbs and behaviors
  • Designer-friendly — Configure everything in Unity's Inspector

docs.title: Quick Example
docs.text:
> look
Kitchen
You are in a small kitchen. A wooden table sits in the center.

> examine table
A sturdy oak table. There's a brass key on it.

> take key
Taken.

> inventory
You are carrying:
  - brass key

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
1. Open the project in Unity
  2. Load Assets/Scenes/SampleScene
  3. Press Play
  4. Type help for available commands

See Getting Started for a full walkthrough.

docs.title: Built-in Actions
docs.text: Action Aliases Description look observe, watch Describe current room examine x, inspect, look at Look closely at something take grab, pick up Add item to inventory go — Move through an exit open — Open a door or container close shut Close a door or container lock — Lock with a key unlock — Unlock with a key inventory i, inv List carried items attack hit, strike, punch Attack something listen hear Listen to surroundings smell sniff Smell something help ?, hint, commands Show available commands

docs.title: System Commands
docs.text: Command Effect quit End game and exit exit Same as quit q Same as quit

docs.title: Text Responses
docs.text:
Simple text shown when action is performed:

  1. Select your object in Inspector
  2. Expand Text Responses
  3. Add entry: Action Keyword = "examine", Response = "It's a rusty old key."

docs.title: Action Restrictions
docs.text:
Block actions with a message:

  1. Expand Action Restrictions
  2. Add entry: Action Keyword = "take", Message = "It's bolted to the floor."

docs.title: Action Overrides
docs.text:
Replace default behavior entirely:

  1. Create a custom Action asset
  2. Expand Action Overrides on your object
  3. Assign your custom action

docs.title: Creating Custom Actions
docs.text:
1. Create a new C# script extending Action
  2. Add [CreateAssetMenu] attribute
  3. Implement required methods
  4. Create asset in Resources/Actions/ or GameWorld/CustomActions/
[CreateAssetMenu(fileName = "Dance", menuName = "IFEngine/Actions/CustomActions/Dance")]
public class Dance : Action
{
    public override string Keyword => "dance";
    public override List<string> Aliases { get; } = new() { "boogie" };
    public override bool CanAffectWorld => false;
    public override ItemApplicabilityLevel ItemApplicabilityLevel => ItemApplicabilityLevel.NA;

    public override bool CanApplyToItem(BaseObject item) => true;

    public override ActionStatus Execute(GameController controller, BaseObject item)
    {
        return ActionHelper.LogActionAndReturnStatus(
            gameController: controller,
            message: "You dance a little jig."
        );
    }
}

docs.title: Objects
docs.text:
Everything in the game world is a BaseObject — rooms, items, characters, doors.

Each object has:

Property Purpose mainName How the player refers to it aliases Alternative names ("key", "brass key") initialAppearance Description shown on first encounter hasBeenInteractedWith Tracks if player has manipulated it

docs.title: Kinds
docs.text:
Specialized object types with built-in behaviors:

Kind Description Room A location with exits, tracks visit count Creature Living entity (player or NPC) Container Holds other objects Door Openable/lockable barrier Exit Connection between rooms Supporter Surface that holds items Scenery Background, non-interactive

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Attachable traits that define what objects can do:

Property Effect Openable Can be opened/closed Lockable Can be locked/unlocked with a key HoldsContents Can contain other objects FixedInPlace Cannot be taken Lightable Can be lit or dark

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Player verbs that interact with the world:

  • Execute: Performs the action, returns success/failure
  • CanApplyToItem: Validates if action works on target
  • CanAffectWorld: If true, triggers hasBeenInteractedWith

docs.title: Game Flow
docs.text:
Player Input → Parser → GameController → Action → Events → Display
  1. Player types a command
  2. Parser extracts action + target
  3. Controller validates and executes
  4. Action generates events
  5. Orchestrator displays results

docs.title: Create a Room
docs.text:
1. Create → IFEngine/Kinds/Room
  2. Set Main Name (how player sees it)
  3. Set Initial Appearance (first visit description)
  4. Add Aliases (e.g., "kitchen", "room")

docs.title: Connect with Exits
docs.text:
1. Create → IFEngine/Kinds/Exit
  2. Set Main Name to direction ("north", "upstairs")
  3. Assign Destination Room
  4. Add Exit to source room's Exits list

docs.title: Add a Door
docs.text:
1. Create → IFEngine/Kinds/Door
  2. Configure Openable and Lockable properties
  3. Assign Door to the Exit

docs.title: Basic Item
docs.text:
1. Create → IFEngine/CoreObjects/BaseObject
  2. Set name and appearance
  3. Add to a room's HoldsContents property

docs.title: Container
docs.text:
1. Create → IFEngine/Kinds/Container
  2. Add items to its HoldsContents
  3. Configure Openable if needed

docs.title: Key
docs.text:
1. Create a BaseObject for the key
  2. On the locked door, set Lockable.Key to your key asset

docs.title: Player
docs.text:
1. Create → IFEngine/Kinds/Creature
  2. Check Is Player
  3. Assign to Orchestrator's Player Character

docs.title: NPCs
docs.text:
1. Create Creature assets
  2. Add to rooms via HoldsContents
  3. Add to Orchestrator's Non Player Characters

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use Initial Appearance for atmospheric first impressions
  • Add Text Responses for "examine" to give item details
  • Use Action Restrictions to block illogical actions
  • Test frequently with help to verify commands work

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Unity 6 or later
  • TextMesh Pro (included)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Download or clone the project
  2. Open in Unity Hub
  3. Let Unity import assets and regenerate Library

docs.title: Running the Sample
docs.text:
1. Open Assets/Scenes/SampleScene
  2. Press Play
  3. Type commands in the input field

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
Assets/
├── Engine/           # Core framework (don't modify)
│   ├── CoreObjects/  # BaseObject, Action base classes
│   ├── Mechanics/    # Actions, Kinds, Properties
│   ├── ControlCentre/# Game logic
│   └── Utils/        # Helpers
├── GameWorld/        # Your game content
│   ├── Rooms/        # Room assets
│   ├── Characters/   # Player and NPCs
│   └── CustomActions/# Game-specific actions
├── Resources/
│   └── Actions/      # Core action assets
└── Scenes/           # Unity scenes

docs.title: Creating Your First Room
docs.text:
1. Right-click in Assets/GameWorld/Rooms/
  2. Select Create → IFEngine/Kinds/Room
  3. Name it (e.g., "Kitchen")
  4. In Inspector, set:
  5. Main Name: Kitchen
  6. Initial Appearance: A small kitchen with checkered tiles...

docs.title: Connecting Rooms
docs.text:
1. Create an Exit asset in your room's folder
  2. Set the Destination Room
  3. Add the Exit to your room's Exits list
  4. Optionally attach a Door for locked passages

docs.title: Setting Up the Orchestrator
docs.text:
Select the Orchestrator in your scene and assign:

  • Starting Room — Where the player begins
  • All Rooms — Every room in your game
  • Player Character — The player's Creature asset
  • Custom Actions — Any game-specific actions

Press Play to test.
